bull_bear.body:
- Made-to-order sectional product range spanning angles, channels, squares, flats and rounds in multiple sizes, giving product diversification within re-bars
- Diversified customer base with a focus on institutional customers, supported by market intelligence and demand forecasting (stated as market-risk mitigation)
- Multiple sourcing strategy and long-term supplier relationships for raw material, with inventory optimisation and continuous procurement monitoring
- ISO 9001:2008 quality certification of the existing manufacturing unit
- Re-casting of the re-heating furnace internal lining of the Structural and TMT Units with latest engineering technology, stated to yield maximum heat with lesser fuel consumption
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Going-concern material uncertainty tied to implementation of the NCLT-approved Resolution Plan — The Secretarial Auditor records that the Statutory Auditors have expressed a material uncertainty relating to the Company's ability to continue as a going concern, dependent on successful implementation of the approved Resolution Plan, generation of adequate cash flows and availability of necessary financial support; instalments aggregating Rs. 21.50 crore payable under the Plan up to March 31, 2026 remained unpaid, as did statutory liabilities of approximately Rs. 85 lakh, and the Successful Resolution Applicant's application to realign payment timelines is pending before the NCLT.
- Raw material price and availability risk — Fluctuations in prices and availability of iron ore, coal, scrap and other inputs may impact profitability; mitigated by a multiple sourcing strategy, long-term supplier relationships, inventory optimisation and continuous procurement monitoring.
- Market / demand risk — Demand fluctuations due to changes in economic conditions, infrastructure spending and industrial production; mitigated by a diversified customer base, focus on institutional customers, product diversification and demand forecasting.
- Import-led pricing pressure and competition — Cheap imports from global markets lead to pricing pressure, and the Company faces intense competition from both organised and unorganised sectors; management cites ICRA's view that steel producers' profitability may remain under pressure from elevated imports and subdued international prices unless trade protection measures are implemented.
- Regulatory risk, including environmental and sustainability compliance — Changes in Government policies, environmental regulations and taxation laws may impact operations, and the Company lists increasing environmental and sustainability compliance requirements among industry threats; mitigated by continuous regulatory monitoring and a compliance framework.
- Financial risk — interest rates, liquidity and credit — Interest rate movements, liquidity management and credit risks remain important considerations; mitigated by conservative treasury practices, efficient working capital management and periodic review of financial exposures. The Secretarial Audit report notes the working capital facility was restructured under the Resolution Plan, with the secured liability reduced from Rs. 82.69 crore to Rs. 47.25 crore.
- Operational risk — equipment, power, logistics and workforce — Equipment failures, power shortages, logistics disruptions and workforce availability may affect operations; mitigated by preventive maintenance, safety management systems, vendor diversification and employee training. High energy and logistics costs are separately flagged as an industry threat.
- Related-party concentration in trading flows — The AOC-2 disclosure shows material sales of goods, purchases of goods and job charges transacted with companies in which KMP or their relatives can exercise significant influence, alongside an interest-free unsecured loan from a Director, concentrating a part of the business with related entities.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

The main application of the products currently manufactured is in the infrastructure and construction industry, and the Company states it serves a diversified customer base with a focus on institutional customers.

outlook.body:
- Focus on operational efficiency and strengthening operational efficiencies
- Improving product quality and customer satisfaction; enhancing customer relationships
- Prudent financial management and maintaining financial discipline
- Strengthening market presence
- Product diversification and a diversified customer base with a focus on institutional customers (stated as market-risk mitigation)
- Multiple sourcing strategy, long-term supplier relationships and inventory optimisation for raw material
- Increasing the level of automation on the production side and method improvements in the manufacturing process
- Energy conservation, including LED plant lighting, power factor correction and use of a recuperator in the rolling mill, with solar adoption in the pipeline
- Implementation of the Resolution Plan approved by the NCLT, Kolkata Bench
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capacity-addition or expansion project for the Company. The only plant-level investment described is technology absorption and energy-conservation work at the existing units: the re-heating furnace internal lining of the Structural Unit and the TMT Unit was re-cast with latest engineering technology to obtain maximum heat yield with lesser fuel consumption, pollution control equipment for air and water was upgraded, automation on the production side was increased, LED lighting was adopted for the entire plant lighting and automatic power factor correction equipment was installed. Adoption of solar energy is stated to be in the pipeline for domestic consumption and common pathway lighting, and rainwater harvesting is being adopted for the manufacturing water requirement during the monsoon. The Company states the capital investment in energy conservation equipment was NIL and that expenditure on research or development was NIL; no fresh technology was imported during the year. Separately, the Company is implementing the Resolution Plan approved by the NCLT Kolkata Bench, under which the Successful Resolution Applicant invested Rs. 2.69 crore through acquisition of a 95% stake, while instalments aggregating Rs. 21.50 crore payable up to March 31, 2026 remained unpaid.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Continued Government capital expenditure and investment in roads, railways, ports, airports and urban infrastructure is expected to sustain steel demand
- Growing demand from housing, commercial construction and industrial development, and increasing urbanisation
- Expansion of renewable energy, transmission and power infrastructure
- Increasing manufacturing activity under 'Make in India' and Government policy support through PLI schemes
- Rising demand for value-added and specialised steel products
- Digitalisation, automation and Industry 4.0 adoption across steel manufacturing
- Management cites ICRA's expectation that domestic finished steel demand will grow 7-8% during FY 2026, supported by ongoing infrastructure development
- Management cites ICRA's view that steel producers' profitability may remain under pressure from elevated imports and subdued international steel prices unless trade protection measures are implemented
- Management cites ICRA's expectation that industry capacity utilisation will improve beyond 80% as producers defer capacity additions in response to softer earnings
- Cheap imports from global markets causing pricing pressure, and volatility in iron ore, coking coal and scrap prices, are flagged as threats to profitability
- High energy and logistics costs and intense competition from organised and unorganised sectors are flagged as threats
- Management states that companies focusing on operational efficiency, value-added products, cost optimisation and prudent capital allocation are expected to remain better positioned

risks.risk: Going-concern material uncertainty tied to implementation of the NCLT-approved Resolution Plan
risks.note: The Secretarial Auditor records that the Statutory Auditors have expressed a material uncertainty relating to the Company's ability to continue as a going concern, dependent on successful implementation of the approved Resolution Plan, generation of adequate cash flows and availability of necessary financial support; instalments aggregating Rs. 21.50 crore payable under the Plan up to March 31, 2026 remained unpaid, as did statutory liabilities of approximately Rs. 85 lakh, and the Successful Resolution Applicant's application to realign payment timelines is pending before the NCLT.

risks.risk: Raw material price and availability risk
risks.note: Fluctuations in prices and availability of iron ore, coal, scrap and other inputs may impact profitability; mitigated by a multiple sourcing strategy, long-term supplier relationships, inventory optimisation and continuous procurement monitoring.

Demand fluctuations due to changes in economic conditions, infrastructure spending and industrial production; mitigated by a diversified customer base, focus on institutional customers, product diversification and demand forecasting.

Cheap imports from global markets lead to pricing pressure, and the Company faces intense competition from both organised and unorganised sectors; management cites ICRA's view that steel producers' profitability may remain under pressure from elevated imports and subdued international prices unless trade protection measures are implemented.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk, including environmental and sustainability compliance
risks.note: Changes in Government policies, environmental regulations and taxation laws may impact operations, and the Company lists increasing environmental and sustainability compliance requirements among industry threats; mitigated by continuous regulatory monitoring and a compliance framework.

risks.risk: Financial risk — interest rates, liquidity and credit
risks.note: Interest rate movements, liquidity management and credit risks remain important considerations; mitigated by conservative treasury practices, efficient working capital management and periodic review of financial exposures. The Secretarial Audit report notes the working capital facility was restructured under the Resolution Plan, with the secured liability reduced from Rs. 82.69 crore to Rs. 47.25 crore.

risks.risk: Operational risk — equipment, power, logistics and workforce
risks.note: Equipment failures, power shortages, logistics disruptions and workforce availability may affect operations; mitigated by preventive maintenance, safety management systems, vendor diversification and employee training. High energy and logistics costs are separately flagged as an industry threat.

The AOC-2 disclosure shows material sales of goods, purchases of goods and job charges transacted with companies in which KMP or their relatives can exercise significant influence, alongside an interest-free unsecured loan from a Director, concentrating a part of the business with related entities.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aanchal Ispat Limited is a Howrah (West Bengal) based hot re-rolling steel manufacturer making mild steel structural re-bars, angles, channels, rounds and other sectional products for the infrastructure and construction industry, operating under a Resolution Plan approved by the NCLT Kolkata Bench.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures mild steel structural re-bars, angles, channels, MS rounds, squares and flats and other sectional products made to order, which are broadly categorised as re-bars within the steel industry. Products are produced through a hot re-rolling process in which mild steel billets are heated and passed through rolling mills to achieve the required cross-section. The main application of the products currently manufactured is in the infrastructure and construction industry, and the Company states it serves a diversified customer base with a focus on institutional customers.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Mild steel structural / sectional products:** Mild Steel Angles (35x35 mm to 75x75 mm), Mild Steel Channels (75x40 mm, 75x50 mm, 100x50 mm), Mild Steel Square (10 mm, 12 mm, 16 mm), Mild Steel Flat, Mild Steel Structural Round Bars, Mild steel structural re-bars and other sectional products as per order

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Infrastructure and construction industry
- Buildings and industrial structures / industrial sheds and warehouses
- Bridges, flyovers and infrastructure projects
- Transmission towers, substation structures and power infrastructure
- General fabrication (gates, grills, fencing, frames, supports, brackets, racks and shelving)
- Automobile, engineering and machinery components
- Agricultural tools and implements
- Domestic market only (foreign exchange earnings and outgo were NIL in FY 2025-26)

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body: ISO 9001:2008 certified from BSCIC Quality Management Systems (existing manufacturing unit)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Continued Government capital expenditure and investment in roads, railways, ports, airports and urban infrastructure is expected to sustain steel demand
- Growing demand from housing, commercial construction and industrial development, and increasing urbanisation
- Expansion of renewable energy, transmission and power infrastructure
- Increasing manufacturing activity under 'Make in India' and Government policy support through PLI schemes
- Rising demand for value-added and specialised steel products
- Digitalisation, automation and Industry 4.0 adoption across steel manufacturing
- Management cites ICRA's expectation that domestic finished steel demand will grow 7-8% during FY 2026, supported by ongoing infrastructure development
- Management cites ICRA's view that steel producers' profitability may remain under pressure from elevated imports and subdued international steel prices unless trade protection measures are implemented
- Management cites ICRA's expectation that industry capacity utilisation will improve beyond 80% as producers defer capacity additions in response to softer earnings
- Cheap imports from global markets causing pricing pressure, and volatility in iron ore, coking coal and scrap prices, are flagged as threats to profitability
- High energy and logistics costs and intense competition from organised and unorganised sectors are flagged as threats
- Management states that companies focusing on operational efficiency, value-added products, cost optimisation and prudent capital allocation are expected to remain better positioned

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Focus on operational efficiency and strengthening operational efficiencies
- Improving product quality and customer satisfaction; enhancing customer relationships
- Prudent financial management and maintaining financial discipline
- Strengthening market presence
- Product diversification and a diversified customer base with a focus on institutional customers (stated as market-risk mitigation)
- Multiple sourcing strategy, long-term supplier relationships and inventory optimisation for raw material
- Increasing the level of automation on the production side and method improvements in the manufacturing process
- Energy conservation, including LED plant lighting, power factor correction and use of a recuperator in the rolling mill, with solar adoption in the pipeline
- Implementation of the Resolution Plan approved by the NCLT, Kolkata Bench

moat.body:
- Made-to-order sectional product range spanning angles, channels, squares, flats and rounds in multiple sizes, giving product diversification within re-bars
